beginner_glossary.Neocloud / AI-native hyperscaler: A new kind of cloud company built specifically to rent out AI computing (mostly NVIDIA GPUs) at huge scale — as opposed to the general-purpose 'hyperscalers' (AWS, Azure, Google) that do everything. Nebius calls itself an 'AI-native hyperscaler'. CoreWeave is the best-known peer.
beginner_glossary.Full-stack AI cloud: Offering not just raw GPU rental ('bare metal') but the whole AI life cycle on top — multi-tenant cloud, inference, agentic tools, and software. Nebius's pitch is that it owns and integrates the WHOLE stack (hardware + software), which it says is rare among neoclouds.
beginner_glossary.GPU: Graphics Processing Unit — the chip (made by NVIDIA) that does the heavy math for AI training and inference. Neoclouds buy these by the hundreds of thousands and rent out the compute.
beginner_glossary.Gigawatt (GW) of power: Data centers are measured by the electrical power they can draw. 1 GW is enormous (a large power plant's output). Nebius had 3.5+ GW of CONTRACTED power and targets 4+ GW by end-2026 — a proxy for how much AI capacity it is building.
beginner_glossary.ARR (Annualized Run-Rate Revenue): Recent revenue projected over a full year — a forward-looking size gauge for a fast-growing business. Nebius's AI business hit a $1.9B ARR by end-Q1 2026 and the company targets $7–9B ARR by the end of 2026.
beginner_glossary.Adjusted EBITDA: Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization, with some items stripped out — a proxy for the cash profitability of the core operations. Nebius's group adjusted EBITDA margin was 32% in Q1 2026 (45% for the core Nebius AI business). This, NOT net income, shows the operating trend.
beginner_glossary.Capex (capital expenditure): Money spent building data centers and buying GPUs. Nebius RAISED its 2026 capex guidance to $20–25 billion — a massive number relative to its revenue, funded by a mix of cash, customer prepayments, debt, and equity.
beginner_glossary.Customer prepayments: Cash customers pay UPFRONT to lock in future capacity. These are huge for Nebius (they drove $2.3B of operating cash flow in Q1 2026) and reduce how much outside financing it needs.
beginner_glossary.Asset-backed financing: Borrowing money secured against a specific asset or contract. Nebius plans to borrow against its long-term Meta and Microsoft contracts (which carry those customers' strong credit), getting cheap debt to build data centers.
beginner_glossary.Convertible notes ('converts'): Bonds that can later convert into shares. Nebius raised $4.3B of converts in Q1 2026 at low coupons (1.25% and ~2.6%) — cheap capital, but potential future share dilution.
beginner_glossary.Token Factory: Nebius's inference product — it runs AI models so customers pay per 'token' (unit of AI output) rather than renting raw GPUs. Strengthened by the Eigen AI and Clarifai acquisitions. Inference is the fastest-growing part of the stack.
beginner_glossary.Inference vs training: TRAINING = teaching an AI model (huge, bursty compute). INFERENCE = running the finished model to answer queries (steadier, fast-growing, where Token Factory plays). Nebius serves both.
beginner_glossary.Agentic / agentic search: AI 'agents' that carry out multi-step tasks autonomously. Nebius bought Tavily to add agentic search; it sees agentic workloads as the next big consumption layer.
beginner_glossary.Vera Rubin / Rubin / GB300: NVIDIA's chip generations. 'GB300' (Blackwell-class) is current; 'Vera Rubin' (Rubin GPU + Vera CPU) is NVIDIA's next platform. Nebius's NVIDIA partnership gives it EARLY access to deploy these.
beginner_glossary.NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status: An NVIDIA certification that a cloud meets top performance standards on a given GPU generation. Nebius earned it on GB300 for training — a quality signal and a sign of its close NVIDIA ties.
beginner_glossary.ClickHouse / Toloka / TripleTen / Avride: Companies Nebius owns stakes in or consolidates (ClickHouse = a fast database, a minority stake; Toloka = data labeling; TripleTen = edtech; Avride = autonomous driving). ClickHouse's rising valuation drove a big NON-CASH net-income gain in Q1 2026.
beginner_glossary.Owned vs leased capacity: Whether Nebius owns its data centers or rents them. Nebius's owned capacity is >75% of its total power — it argues owning the full stack makes it more efficient.
beginner_glossary.P/E vs EV/Revenue: P/E (price ÷ earnings) is not useful here because earnings are distorted by non-cash gains. Investors instead use revenue/ARR multiples (e.g., market value ÷ revenue) to value fast-growing, capital-heavy cloud companies.

company_snapshot.what_it_is: Nebius is an 'AI-native hyperscaler' — a neocloud that builds large data centers, fills them with NVIDIA GPUs, and rents AI computing plus a full software stack (inference 'Token Factory', agentic tools, multi-tenant cloud). In the AI/semiconductor supply chain it is a CLOUD / NEOCLOUD node: a huge buyer of NVIDIA accelerators (now also a $2B NVIDIA equity investee) that hosts AI workloads for AI-native startups, enterprises, and big tech (Meta, Microsoft as capacity customers). It emerged in 2024 from the international assets of the former Yandex N.V. (after Yandex's Russian businesses were divested) and is led by Yandex co-founder Arkady Volozh.
company_snapshot.headquarters: Amsterdam, Netherlands (data centers across the U.S. and Europe)
company_snapshot.founder_ceo: Founder & CEO: Arkady Volozh (co-founder of Yandex). CFO: Dado Alonso. Key execs: Andrey Korolenko (infrastructure), Marc Boroditsky (go-to-market/CRO), Roman Chernin (product/software).
company_snapshot.founded: 2024 as Nebius Group N.V. (relaunched from the international assets of the former Yandex N.V.; AI-cloud roots predate the rename)
company_snapshot.manufacturing_footprint: Builds and largely OWNS its data centers (>75% of total power is owned, contracted capacity). U.S. sites include a new Pennsylvania campus (1.2 GW once fully live), plus Alabama, Missouri (Independence), and New Jersey (Vineland) projects; also European capacity. Contracted power 3.5+ GW, targeting 4+ GW by end-2026. [Q1 2026 call 2026-05-13]
end_markets: Enterprises (fintech, life sciences, manufacturing, energy, pharma)

business_model.summary: Nebius makes money by renting AI computing at scale. It raises capital, builds (mostly owned) data centers, fills them with NVIDIA GPUs, and sells that capacity — from raw 'bare metal' to multi-tenant cloud to inference (Token Factory) to agentic tools. Demand currently exceeds supply, so it 'sells out' everything it builds and is even able to raise prices. The economic engine is: pre-sell capacity (often with upfront prepayments and long-term contracts like Meta/Microsoft) → use those contracts to raise cheap, asset-backed financing → build more capacity → repeat. The whole model is a capital-intensive bet that AI compute demand keeps outrunning supply.
how_they_make_money: Core AI cloud (Nebius AI): renting GPU compute and full-stack cloud services to a diversified base of AI startups and enterprises — 98% of group revenue in Q1 2026; this is the priority business. [Q1 2026 call]
Strategic capacity contracts: large, long-term deals with big tech (Meta $27B/5yr; Microsoft) that anchor financing and revenue visibility. [Q1 2026 call]

Inference / software (Token Factory): pay-per-token inference plus agentic tools (strengthened by Eigen AI, Clarifai, Tavily acquisitions) — software as an 'enabler' that pulls more compute consumption. [Q1 2026 call]

Other consolidated/minority holdings: TripleTen (edtech), Avride (autonomous driving), and stakes such as ClickHouse and Toloka — small in revenue but a source of (non-cash) valuation gains. [Q1 2026 call]
competitive_moat_analyst_view: Full-stack ownership: Nebius owns hardware + software and >75% of its capacity, arguing this yields better efficiency, total cost of ownership, and unit economics than asset-light rivals. [Q1 2026 call]

Privileged NVIDIA relationship: a $2B NVIDIA equity investment, line of sight to 5 GW by 2030, early access to Rubin/Vera platforms, and 'Exemplar Cloud' status across multiple GPU generations — supply-chain certainty when GPUs are scarce. [Q1 2026 call]
Anchor contracts as a financing engine: Meta/Microsoft deals let Nebius raise cheap asset-backed debt against strong customer credit, funding the build-out at attractive rates. [Q1 2026 call]
Deep engineering talent + selective M&A: roots in Yandex's engineering culture, plus tuck-in acquisitions (Eigen, Clarifai, Tavily) to speed the software roadmap.

ASSUMPTION-flavored: these advantages are real but the neocloud model is fundamentally capital- and execution-intensive; the 'moat' depends on continued cheap capital access and demand staying ahead of supply.

revenue_streams.analyst_view: Nebius is essentially ONE business — the Nebius AI neocloud (98% of revenue) — wrapped around a few investment holdings. The core is growing at triple digits, selling out everything it builds, raising prices, and inflecting to real operating profitability (45% AI adjusted-EBITDA margin). The Meta/Microsoft deals are best understood as FINANCING and visibility anchors more than the main event; management is explicit that the diversified AI-cloud book is the priority. The holdings (ClickHouse, etc.) add reported-earnings noise but little revenue — which is exactly why this stock must be judged on revenue/ARR/EBITDA, not net income.

competitors.landscape_summary: Nebius competes in the fast-growing 'neocloud' space — specialized AI-compute providers — against both the giant general hyperscalers and a field of AI-specialist clouds. Its differentiation is full-stack ownership (hardware + software, >75% owned capacity) and a privileged NVIDIA relationship, versus more compute-only or asset-light rivals.

competitors.differentiation_analyst_view: Nebius's edge is being a FULL-STACK, mostly-owned AI cloud with deep engineering talent and an unusually close NVIDIA tie — it sells more than bare GPUs (inference, agentic, software) to a diversified customer base, not just a few big offtakers. Its disadvantages are scale and capital access relative to the trillion-dollar hyperscalers, and the inherent fragility of a model that depends on continuous cheap financing. The competitive question is less 'is there demand' (there clearly is) and more whether Nebius can keep funding and executing the build-out faster and cheaper than rivals.

financial_performance.analyst_view: The operating trajectory is extraordinary: revenue +684% YoY, ARR to $1.9B (and guided to $7–9B by year-end), and a real margin inflection (group adj. EBITDA from -$54M a year ago to +$130M, 32% margin; AI business at 45%). The reported NET INCOME, however, is mostly a non-cash ClickHouse mark and should be ignored for valuation. The make-or-break variable is FINANCING: Nebius must fund $20–25B of 2026 capex, and it is doing so cleverly (prepayments, $4.3B cheap converts, $2B NVIDIA equity, asset-backed debt on Meta/Microsoft credit, $9.3B cash). If capital stays cheap and capacity converts to ARR on schedule, the model compounds; if capital markets tighten or demand softens, the same leverage cuts the other way.

valuation.analyst_view: NBIS is a high-beta, high-conviction-on-both-sides AI-infrastructure stock. The bull case: a full-stack, NVIDIA-backed neocloud selling out everything it builds, inflecting to strong adjusted-EBITDA margins, with ARR potentially 5–7x-ing in a year and creative financing in place. The bear case: it must raise and deploy tens of billions flawlessly, depends on cheap capital and demand staying ahead of supply, carries big-customer concentration (Meta/Microsoft) and a Yandex-legacy/holding structure, and trades on forward ARR with a low-$120s analyst floor implying ~50% downside. The debate is squarely about FINANCING + EXECUTION risk versus a real, fast-growing operating business — not about whether AI-cloud demand exists.

risks.why_it_matters: Nebius must fund $20–25B of 2026 capex; if debt/equity markets tighten or terms worsen, the build-out (and the ARR ramp) stalls — the single biggest risk.
Growth is back-end-weighted and depends on power, sites, and on-time data-center delivery; delays (e.g., reported Vineland NJ questions) push out revenue.
Meta and Microsoft are very large contracts; over-reliance on a few big offtakers raises risk if one pulls back (mitigated by a diversified AI-cloud book).
The model assumes demand keeps exceeding supply and prices hold/rise; an AI-capex digestion or a flood of new GPU supply would hit utilization and pricing hard.
Nebius's roadmap, supply, and even its cap table are tied to NVIDIA; any shift in NVIDIA allocation, pricing, or strategy would matter a lot.
Reported net income is distorted by non-cash marks on ClickHouse/Toloka/etc.; the Yandex-legacy structure and minority stakes make the financials harder to read and value.
Priced on forward ARR (~7–8x) with a 52-week range of $44–$279 and an analyst floor near $120; any stumble can cause large drawdowns.
Convertible notes and the at-the-market equity program can dilute shareholders if used, especially if the stock falls.
Local pushback, permitting, and power constraints can slow or block capacity additions.
AWS/Azure/Google/Oracle and CoreWeave et al. have more scale/capital; competition could pressure pricing and customer wins over time.

final_research_summary.one_paragraph: Nebius Group (NBIS) is an 'AI-native hyperscaler' — a neocloud that builds mostly-owned, gigawatt-scale data centers, fills them with NVIDIA GPUs, and rents AI compute plus a full software stack (inference 'Token Factory', agentic tools). It emerged in 2024 from the international assets of the former Yandex N.V., is run by Yandex co-founder Arkady Volozh, and sits in the AI supply chain as a major NVIDIA-buyer/neocloud (now also a $2B NVIDIA equity investee). The operating ramp is extraordinary: FY2025 revenue was US$529.8M (+351%) with ~US$1.25B ARR, and Q1 2026 (reported 2026-05-13) delivered group revenue US$399M (+684% YoY), Nebius AI revenue US$390M (+841%), ARR of US$1.9B, and a real margin inflection (group adjusted EBITDA US$130M / 32% margin, the AI business at 45%) — while selling out all capacity and raising prices. It signed a US$27B/5-year Meta deal ($12B dedicated + $15B optional capacity), has a Microsoft contract, and raised over US$6B in 2026 (US$4.3B cheap converts + US$2B NVIDIA equity), ending Q1 with US$9.3B cash; it then RAISED 2026 capex guidance to US$20–25B to build 2027 capacity. Crucially, reported NET INCOME (US$621M in Q1, US$817M TTM) is mostly a NON-CASH ClickHouse valuation gain, so the ~80x P/E is meaningless — the stock (US$232, ~US$59.5B market cap, 52-week range US$44–$279) must be judged on revenue/ARR: ~18x FY2026 guided revenue and ~7–8x the US$7–9B 2026 EXIT ARR. What is FACT is a hyper-growth, NVIDIA-backed, margin-inflecting neocloud with strong demand and creative financing; what is being PRICED is flawless execution of a US$20–25B build-out funded by continuously cheap capital. The real debate is FINANCING + EXECUTION risk (and an enormous US$120–$380 analyst-target spread), not whether AI-cloud demand is real.
